using.title: Using the App
steps: Drag the white strip sideways. It snaps so that each note lands exactly under one mode column. Left moves by fourths; right moves by fifths.
The note under the grade marked 1 is the tonic. By default that is Ionian (Major). Tap a mode name to make that column grade 1 instead.
Ionian is the common Major scale; Aeolian is the common Minor. Both are labelled on the board.
Read down any column to get the chord built on that note: its triad, then its seventh chord.
Slide one column to the right to add a sharp to the key, one to the left to add a flat.
Use Share to copy a link that reopens the exact position and tonic mode you are looking at.
On a keyboard: left and right arrows move one column; Page Up and Page Down jump a whole block of seven; Home and End go to the far ends of the strip.

sections.heading: What scale are you looking to build?
sections.body: Pick a tonic and bring it to the mode you are looking for. The notes left in view are the ones that make up your field.
sections.example: E.g.: if you want to play in D Lydian, just bring the note D to the Lydian cell; you are left with 3 altered sounds: F#, C#, and G#.

sections.heading: Modulations
sections.body: Nudge the field slightly — left by fourths or right by fifths — to quickly visualize nearby modulations.

sections.heading: Staying in a mode
sections.body: Try moving the field so you stay in the same mode even as you change the note.
